title: Horizontal Fitting Selection: Sanitary Tee vs. Combination Wye
description: Using a short-turn sanitary tee in a horizontal drain line is a frequent code violation that causes chronic clogs. Sanitary tees are engineered for transitions from horizontal to vertical flow, allowing gravity to pull waste downward effectively. When installed horizontally, the sharp turn slows down solid waste flow, leading to buildup and blockages. For horizontal-to-horizontal drainage connections, code requires long-turn fittings such as a combination wye and eighth bend or a long-sweep turn. This maintains waste velocity, prevents solid drop-out, and ensures compliance with standard drain-waste-vent (DWV) installation principles. Always consult local plumbing codes for specific fitting allowance rules.

Horizontal Fitting Selection: Sanitary Tee vs. Combination Wye

Using a short-turn sanitary tee in a horizontal drain line is a frequent code violation that causes chronic clogs. Sanitary tees are engineered for transitions from horizontal to vertical flow, allowing gravity to pull waste downward effectively. When installed horizontally, the sharp turn slows down solid waste flow, leading to buildup and blockages. For horizontal-to-horizontal drainage connections, code requires long-turn fittings such as a combination wye and eighth bend or a long-sweep turn. This maintains waste velocity, prevents solid drop-out, and ensures compliance with standard drain-waste-vent (DWV) installation principles. Always consult local plumbing codes for specific fitting allowance rules.
